decisions.reason: The routing constraints mention the USB-C and battery connectors only as endpoints of high-current paths; they do not change connector placement, accessibility, enclosure fit, or antenna-layout requirements.
The 3.2 A VBUS and BAT- routing requirements do not affect the independently specified display-backlight circuit or its approximately 140 mA load.

The source constrains integrated-board copper routing from the battery connector to the AXP2101 but does not change the power-board battery connector's type, pinout, placement, voltage range, or destination.

The source uses simultaneous charging and system load to establish a routing-current basis, but it does not change the selected AXP2101 architecture, required rails, charging behavior, or efficiency goal.
Copper-pour continuity and stitching-via requirements for VBUS and BAT- do not change the local placement requirements for AXP2101 or MT3608 decoupling capacitors.
The source concerns high-current VBUS and BAT routing, not the signal-only PWROK, VBACKUP, or VRTC auxiliary-pin configuration.
The routing acceptance criteria do not revise the cost goal, component-tier preference, connector reduction, or sourcing exception.
The source addresses integrated-board VBUS and BAT- routing under simultaneous charging and load, not the main board's standalone USB-powered 3.3 V LDO mode.
The high-current routing decision does not affect the button and switch pull-ups, active-low behavior, or connector grounding.
Although both requirements involve the AXP2101, the source changes integrated-board high-current routing criteria and does not alter the power-board VMID/VSYS topology or thermal-pad requirement.
The VBUS and BAT- routing constraints do not change the addressable LEDs' 3.3 V supply, direct data drive, model, or separated power control.
The stated 3.2 A worst-case current is a design basis for copper routing, not a change to the required current-measurement capability or the conditional omission of a separate INA device.
